text:
Maya: FYI — noticed sustained SM occupancy spike on the p4d pool for /generate-qa route starting ~01:10UTC. VRAM climbed from ~26GB -> ~39GB over ~20m and token tail latency increased. :eyes:

Alex: Any kernel-selector or runtime rolling changes last night?

Maya: There was a kernel-selector rollout that switched default kernel profile for our Llama-2-13b sequence workloads to fused_matmul_v2 at 01:12UTC (kernel-selector v2.5). Release note: more aggressive fused kernels for mixed fp16 paths. Link: https://internal/release/ks-v2.5 

Sam: Could also be KV cache prefetch behavior + new kernel's memory pattern. Do we have per-request KV cache hit rates and prefix cache evictions around the spike? Grafana?

Maya: Pasted quick query dump from metrics (1m resolution):
```
time,route,kv_hit_rate,sm_occupancy,vram_gb,tail_token_latency_ms
01:05,/generate-qa,0.82,34,26.1,11.2
01:12,/generate-qa,0.78,61,28.5,13.0
01:20,/generate-qa,0.69,78,39.0,18.6
01:30,/generate-qa,0.71,64,30.2,12.8
```

Maya: Notice kv_hit_rate dips then VRAM jumps and SM occupancy follows.

Toni: That looks like prefetch thrashing — prefetch might allocate large temporary buffers which with fused kernel leads to VRAM pressure. Any MIG-slice noise?

Maya: Checked MIG slices on node-id gpu-23: no slice reassigns, but power and thermal climbed a bit: power 280W -> 320W, temp 67C -> 75C.

Erin: Did token-level latency breakdown change? We track kernel + queuing + kv-lookup contributions per token in the token-latency view.

Maya: Yes — kernel execution % of token latency went up (median +8%, p95 +14%). KV lookup latency slightly up but smaller.

Sam: Could be that fused_matmul_v2 uses larger workspace per invocation which increases VRAM working set and reduces effective KV cache capacity (more evictions) -> lower kv_hit -> more recompute.

Alex: Good hypothesis. Can you surface the kernel selection log lines from the runtime profiler around 01:10-01:30? We want to see which kernels were chosen for seq lengths and batch sizes.

Maya: Pulled a few lines from runtime profiler:
```
[01:11:58] choose_kernel(model=llama-13b, seq=1024, batch=1) -> fused_matmul_v2 (workspace=420MB)
[01:12:03] choose_kernel(model=llama-13b, seq=512, batch=2)  -> fused_matmul_v2 (workspace=210MB)
[01:17:42] choose_kernel(model=llama-13b, seq=128, batch=8)  -> scalar_matmul_accel (workspace=48MB)
```

Maya: Notice workspace numbers — the new kernel uses larger workspace for long sequences.

Toni: That explains VRAM growth. If multiple concurrent long seq requests land on same GPU we run out and start evicting KV pages.

Erin: Action plan candidates: 1) rollback kernel-selector to v2.4, 2) limit fused_matmul_v2 to sequences > 2048 only, 3) adjust KV prefetch thresholds, or 4) add per-GPU reservation for KV pages.

Sam: Quick mitigation: pin /generate-qa route to kernel-selector policy v2.4 until we triage. Easiest to revert at runtime.

Alex: Agree. Can we patch the rollout to exclude p4d pool (or specific instance tags) while we instrument more?

Maya: Rolling back kernel-selector on the production rollout now for the p4d cluster: running command:
```
deploy-bot run rollback kernel-selector v2.5 --target p4d-cluster --reason "vram spike on /generate-qa"
```
deploy-bot: rollback started for kernel-selector v2.5 -> v2.4 on target p4d-cluster. Monitoring... :rocket:

Maya: After rollback, VRAM stabilized within 4m on the two affected machines. SM occupancy dropped back to 36-40% and tail latency reduced ~11% at p95.

Toni: For next steps we should: create instrumentation tracking per-token kernel workspace allocation, add a dashboard panel correlating per-route kernel workspace sum vs kv cache occupancy, and run a small-scale perf test with fused_matmul_v2 where we artificially cap concurrency to surface eviction threshold.

Erin: I'll open a ticket for the instrumentation + dashboard and assign to eng-runtime. Ticket: RH-4092. Include queries and example traces.

Sam: Also add a guard in kernel-selector to estimate expected workspace given seq and batch and fall back to lower-workspace kernel if remaining VRAM < X margin. That could avoid these surprises.

Alex: Good. Also we need an alert rule: if per-GPU kv_cache_evictions_rate > 5/min and sm_occupancy > 70% mark as critical.

Maya: Created the Grafana alert rule PR and wired it to #incidents. Link: https://internal/grafana/alert/1123

Erin: Ticket RH-4092 created and linked to the rollback PR + perf run plan.

Sam: I'll own a small benchmark to reproduce with seq=1024 batch=1..4 and run both kernels, capture workspace allocations, kv_hit_rate, and token tail latency. Plan to run tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

Maya: Thanks everyone. Leaving the thread open — will post the perf run results and the dashboards once available. :thumbsup:

metrics-bot: Alert created: grafana/vram-kv-evict-high (id=1123) -> notified #incidents and #eng-runtime.

Erin: Closing loop — please add any missing traces or profiler snippets to RH-4092.

Alex: Nice quick rollback/action. Good catch on TV of kernel workspace. :clap:
